reply.thought: Before recording any payout I need to check the refunds table against Alpha's report. W2 says refunds for orders 235 and 234 applied and order 231 failed, so I'll compare the ledger to that.
The refunds table matches W2's report: orders 234 and 235 are recorded, and 231 is absent as reported. Nothing conflicts, so I can proceed. Next I need the customer list from the orders table.
The refunds table matches W2's report: 234 and 235 are recorded, and 231 is absent as reported. Next I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.

acme's net balance is 36083, which matches its orders (18974 + 17109) with no refunds. Next I'll get birch's net balance. Its order 231 refund failed, so the figure should reflect only the applied refund on 234.

birch's net balance of 28695 matches its orders (21055 + 11644 = 32699) minus the applied refund on 234 (4004), with no deduction for the unrecorded refund on 231. The last customer is cobalt, so I'll get its net balance next.

Cobalt's net balance is 29267, which matches its orders (14171 + 16756 = 30927) minus the applied refund on 235 (1660). All three balances reconcile with the refunds table, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme.
acme's payout of 36083 is recorded. birch's net balance of 28695 reconciles with its orders minus the applied refund on 234, so I'll record that payout next.
Cobalt's payout is the only one left. Its net balance of 29267 reconciles with its orders (30927) minus the applied refund on 235 (1660), so I'll record it.

All three payouts were recorded successfully. Each amount matched its net balance and reconciled against the orders and the applied refunds (234 and 235). Refund 231 was not recorded, and birch's balance correctly excludes it.
